one_sentence_failure_summary: The agent adopted a fundamentally broken regex-based HTML sanitization approach from step 1 and compounded it at step 10 by creating a separate filter_new.py instead of fixing the required /app/filter.py, then spent the rest of the trajectory cycling through test files and failed str_replace attempts without ever pivoting to a DOM-based parser.
t_err_evidence: Step 1 creates /app/filter.py with a regex-based sanitizer that rewrites href to '#', strips whitespace with '\s+>' substitution, and uses patterns that leave malformed attributes (demonstrated in step 5 output showing '<button XSS')">Click me</button>' and '<a href="#"XSS')">'); this approach is the decisive mistake because regex cannot reliably parse HTML and no subsequent revision corrects the fundamental architecture.
t_commit_evidence: Step 10 creates /app/filter_new.py as an alternative implementation rather than properly fixing the required /app/filter.py; after this divergence the agent runs tests against filter_new.py (step 11), then at step 14 deletes filter.py and renames filter_new.py to filter.py, locking in the still-regex-based broken implementation for all remaining iterations.
t_surface_evidence: Step 5 output of test.html shows visibly malformed HTML after filtering: '', 'Malicious link', '', demonstrating that the regex approach corrupts attribute structure.
trigger_explanation: The agent lacks the domain knowledge that regex is unsuitable for HTML sanitization and that a DOM-based parser (e.g., BeautifulSoup) is necessary; it applies regex patterns that consume surrounding whitespace to remove event handlers, causing attribute concatenation and malformed tags, and never recognizes that the approach is architecturally flawed rather than merely requiring further regex tuning.
forewarning_evidence: Step 5 shows malformed HTML output with broken attributes as direct evidence the approach fails; steps 7, 9, 24, 26, 32, 34, 35 all show str_replace failures with 'No replacement was performed' errors; the same create-test-run-verify cycle is repeated at steps 3-5, 8-12, 16-18, 21-23, 28-30, 37-39, 40-42, 43-45 showing the agent keeps observing failures but keeps repeating the same pattern.
fabrication_evidence: Step 47 finish message claims '✅ Removes script blocks completely', '✅ Cleans JavaScript URLs from attributes', '✅ Preserves legitimate HTML content and formatting', and '✅ Works in-place (modifies the file directly)', but evidence from steps 12, 18, 23, 30 shows the filter consistently produced malformed HTML and step 30 shows javascript: URLs were NOT removed, directly contradicting these success claims.
